issues.body: `_workflow_run_shell` iterates over `body.splitlines()` and calls `pipefail_delta` on segments from each physical line. For a body containing `set +o pipefail`, then `set -o \` on one line and `pipefail` on the next, Bash re-enables pipefail, but neither segment matches a complete option transition. The scanner consequently leaves `pipefail` false and suppresses a subsequent `producer | head -1` pipeline. The new fixture asserts same-line separators and scoped constructs, but does not exercise this multiline logical-command bypass, so its exact count remains green despite the false-negative path.
issues.fix_hint: Track pipefail option transitions over shell logical commands, including backslash continuations, before deciding whether following commands are emitted. Add a positive-control fixture that disables pipefail, re-enables it with `set -o \` plus `pipefail` on the next physical line, then contains a vulnerable pipeline, and require that pipeline to be counted.
issues.title: Backslash-continued pipefail re-enable still bypasses the workflow guard

verdict.summary: The round-4 major finding remains unresolved. `_workflow_run_shell` still processes each physical line independently, and `pipefail_delta` only recognizes a complete `set ... pipefail` within one segment. Bash logical commands may span backslash continuations, so `set +o pipefail`, then `set -o \` followed by `pipefail`, re-enables pipefail at runtime while the scanner retains its disabled state. A later vulnerable pipeline is therefore blanked and the real-workflow guard can report a false-clean zero. The expanded control fixture still has no backslash-continuation positive control.
